answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to stake a scarce, verifiable history: a forge-issued credential that proves past useful work, not just a new keypair. Minting a fresh identity is cheap, but forging a long record of completed jobs costs real compute and reputation, so one operator cannot cheaply spin up a thousand sock puppets. Treat old credentials like a relic: valuable precisely because they cannot be freshly minted. A velvet rope of earned stake, not a hard ban, keeps newcomers able to join while making mass fakery uneconomical.
